The papersThe code

Robust Poisson against outliers, dug back up.

Chen, Shi, Qian and Azen asked which model for relative risks holds up when a few outcomes are recorded wrong. Their SAS program was never released. We rebuilt the simulation from the paper and ran all 24 scenarios again. 863 of 864 printed table cells came back within Monte Carlo error.

See every resultSee Fig. 1
Chen et al. 2014BMC Med Res Methodol 14:82 Robust Poisson and log-binomial models with outliers
  1. Fig. 1Inconclusive
  2. Table 1Agrees
  3. Table 2Agrees

  6. The textAgrees
In the overlay, ink is theirs and green is ours

Fig. 1A

Relative bias (%) of the log RR by contamination rate, n = 1500. Log-binomial blue and solid, robust Poisson red and dashed. Rows RR 1.5 and 2.0, columns outcome 10, 25 and 40%. Linear Z, moderate association.

Agrees
Fig. 1A, relative bias, linear Z, moderate association (n = 1500)
95.8% of the lines within 2 px (pass 95%, best control 73.6%), Agrees

Ours scores 0.958 against a pass mark of 0.95; the best wrong input scores 0.175 and the best near miss 0.736. At 2 px a pixel score cannot resolve Monte Carlo noise: one point of relative bias is 4.62 px, and the Monte Carlo SE of a 1,000-replicate relative bias is 0.3 to 1.3 points. Two runs of our own simulation with different seeds score only 0.741 against each other in this panel, while the paper's own Table 1 drawn with the same code scores 0.983, so the drawing and the frame are right. The values behind the panel are Table 1: its 36 values for this panel are each within tolerance and sit at an RMS z of 0.43 from the paper's, where our two runs sit at 0.84 from each other.

Discussion: COPY converged in all fits of 48 of 48 linear and 30 of 48 non-linear scenariosPartly agrees1 of 2 values within tolerance
  • Linear Z: scenarios with every log-binomial fit converged (of 48): paper 48, ours 48
  • Non-linear Z: scenarios with every log-binomial fit converged (of 48): paper 30, ours 48
Every log-binomial fit of ours converges, plain or COPY, so ours counts 48 of 48 non-linear scenarios against the paper's 30. The paper's failures are failures of SAS GENMOD's optimizer on the COPY data, which we cannot run. The boundary that COPY handles is common in our non-linear runs: COPY is needed in some fit of 47 of 48 non-linear scenarios (up to 863 of 1,000 fits, median 172) and of 5 of 48 linear ones (at most 2 fits), which agrees with the paper's split between the forms but cannot say which 18 failed.
Main claim: comparable models with a linear Z; robust Poisson less biased with a quadratic Z from 2% contamination onAgrees2 of 2 values within tolerance
  • Linear Z: LB and RP |bias| within 2 points in every contaminated cell except outcome 10% at 5%: paper yes, ours yes
  • Non-linear Z: RP less biased than LB in every contaminated cell, from 2% on (24): paper yes, ours yes
Discussion: results cited from Petersen and Deddens (three decimals with 10,000 copies; 70% to 100% convergence)Not attemptedResults of another paper, quoted in the Discussion; this paper does not compute them.
Each statement of the text recomputed from the paper's own tablesAgrees18 of 19 statements follow from the paper's own tables. Not: text.se_uncontaminated: Table 2, 0% rows: LB and RP SEs equal at the 2nd decimal in all 24 pairs (yes against no).
robustrr's fits against statsmodels and an independent maximizerAgrees60 contaminated data sets (8 COPY fits): robust Poisson coefficients equal statsmodels' to 1.2e-12 and the sandwich SE its HC0 SE to a relative 3.1e-12; log-binomial coefficients equal an independent maximizer's to 1.0e-06, with a likelihood at least as high (to 1.1e-13) and a score of at most 4.0e-06
The authors' SAS 9.2 program and COPY macroNot attemptedThe simulation program was never released, and the revised COPY macro of Petersen and Deddens is not online (its NIOSH page answers 403). Both are SAS, which no free runtime runs. The method is implemented from the paper's text and checked against its printed tables.
Python package robustrr and its tutorialAgreesrobustrr 0.1.0: wheel installed in a fresh environment and imported from it; tests 8 passed; tutorial 6 cells compared, 0 skipped (nondeterministic); TUTORIAL.md in sync

The main claim holds. Every statement about bias, SE and MSE holds on our run but one, which the paper's own Table 2 breaks as well: without contamination the two SEs differ by less than 0.0009, yet they can round to different second decimals. The one table cell that misses is a misprint in Table 3, and the convergence count of the Discussion belongs to SAS, which we cannot run.

What came back

The simulation
All 24 scenarios at n = 1500 and n = 500, rebuilt as the Python package robustrr and run again with 1,000 replicates each.
The tables
863 of 864 printed cells within Monte Carlo error. The one miss is Table 3 printing 0.013 where its own bias and SE give 0.0351; ours is 0.0357.
The contamination rule
Records past fixed quantiles of p_y are flipped, so how many are flipped varies from data set to data set. Flipping a fixed number in every data set makes the SEs too small at outcome 10%.
Fig. 1
Drawn on the published picture. Panel A passes the 2 px test. B and D fall short of it and C cannot be told from a near miss, while every value behind them is within Monte Carlo tolerance: two of our own runs pass the same test no better.
The claims
Robust Poisson is less biased than log-binomial in every contaminated cell with a quadratic confounder, and the two are within 2 points with a linear one except at outcome 10% and 5% contamination.

What stayed buried

  • The authors' SAS 9.2 program and the revised COPY macro.
  • Which 18 non-linear scenarios SAS failed to fit. Every fit of ours converges.

The main claim holds. Every statement about bias, SE and MSE holds on our run but one, which the paper's own Table 2 breaks as well: without contamination the two SEs differ by less than 0.0009, yet they can round to different second decimals. The one table cell that misses is a misprint in Table 3, and the convergence count of the Discussion belongs to SAS, which we cannot run.
